properties.title: Azure Virtual Desktop Automated Host Pool Deployment

options.text: Automated host pools use a preview Azure Virtual Desktop API and are currently supported only in Azure Commercial. Azure Virtual Desktop creates, updates, and replaces the session-host virtual machines.
Before deployment, create the session-host subnet and an RBAC-enabled Key Vault containing the required VM administrator secrets. Domain-joined hosts also require domain-join credential secrets.

elements.name: identifier
elements.label: Host Pool Persona
elements.toolTip: A short identifier for the user persona served by this host pool, such as finance, dev, or kiosk.

validations.message: The identifier must begin and end with an alphanumeric character and can contain letters, numbers, underscores, dashes, and dots.

options.text: The Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization resource provider is not registered in this subscription.

validations.message: The friendly name cannot exceed 64 characters.
The friendly name cannot exceed 20 characters.

allowedValues.label: Depth-first
allowedValues.description: Fills a session host to its session limit before using the next available host.

allowedValues.label: Breadth-first
allowedValues.description: Distributes new sessions across all available session hosts.

options.text: Dynamic autoscaling is preview functionality. The deployment assigns Desktop Virtualization Power On Off Contributor and Desktop Virtualization Virtual Machine Contributor to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal at subscription scope. Session hosts must reach wvdhpustgr0prod.blob.core.windows.net.

elements.name: networkSecurityGroup
elements.label: Session Host Network Security Group
elements.toolTip: Optional. Select the network security group that Azure Virtual Desktop should attach to session-host NICs.

validations.message: Use letters, numbers, and dashes; do not begin with a dash or use only numbers.

elements.name: sessionHostCount
elements.label: Desired Session Host Count
elements.toolTip: The final number of session hosts to provision. The deployment internally creates the host pool with zero hosts, deploys storage and policy, and then provisions this requested capacity.
